entries.title: Joel 1:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Came to Joel - Probably in the latter end of Jeroboam the second's reign over Israel and in the days of Uzziah, over Judah.

entries.title: Joel 1:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Old men - The oldest among you, who can remember things done many years ago.

entries.title: Joel 1:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Palmer - worm - Four sorts of insects, are here mentioned, which succeeded each other, and devoured all that might be a support to the Jews, whence ensued a grievous famine.

entries.title: Joel 1:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Is cut off - Suddenly cut off even when you are ready to drink it, and totally cut off by these devouring vermin.

entries.title: Joel 1:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A nation - An innumerable multitude of locusts and caterpillars, called a nation here, as Solomon calls the conies and the ant, Prov 30:25,26, and perhaps a prognostick of a very numerous and mighty nation, that ere long will invade Judah. Strong - Mighty in power, and undaunted in courage, if you refer it to the Assyrian or Babylonians; if to those vermin, they are, though each weak by itself, yet in those multitudes, strong and irresistible. A great lion - Such waste as lions make, these the locusts do, and the Assyrians will make.

entries.title: Joel 1:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The husband of her youth - Espoused to her, but snatched away by an untimely death.

entries.title: Joel 1:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The drink - offering - By the destruction of the vines, all wine (out of which they ought to offer the drink - offering) failed.

entries.title: Joel 1:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The corn - The wheat and barley, is eaten up in its greenness. Dried up - The drought was so great, that the vines were withered, and all their hopes of new wine cut off. The oil - The olive - trees. Languisheth - This is a plain account of the reason why the priests were called to mourn, and why the meal - offering and drink - offering were cut off.

entries.title: Joel 1:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Be ye ashamed - This is a just cause why you should lament and enquire why God is so displeased with you.

entries.title: Joel 1:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sanctify ye - Ye priests, set apart a day wherein to afflict yourselves, confess your sins, and sue out your pardon. Into the house - The courts of the temple, where the people were wont to pray.

entries.title: Joel 1:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The day of the Lord - A day of greater trouble than yet they felt, troubles which God will heap upon them. Shall it come - Unless fasting, prayers and amendment prevent.

entries.title: Joel 1:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Cut off - Devoured by locusts, or withered with drought.

entries.title: Joel 1:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Laid desolate - Run to ruin because the owners discouraged with the barrenness of the seasons, would not repair them.

entries.title: Joel 1:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The fire - The immoderate heats. The wilderness - The world, only means places not ploughed, and less inhabited than others.

entries.title: Joel 1:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Cry - They utter their complaints, their sad tones, they have a voice to cry, as well as an eye to look to God.
